text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-pool-eu-west-1 saturation detected. queue_depth=2387, avg_latency=1423ms, scale_attempts=3 (last 7m). Autoscaler health: Unhealthy (crashloop 2/3). Paging on-call.
ingrid: ack — I'm on it, grabbing context.
dmitri: i'm oncall, jumping in. can anyone confirm whether this is localized to eu-west-1 or multi-region?
maria: dashboards show eu-west-1 only. us-west and eu-central healthy.
kevin: seeing a spike of small request bursts from a new partner integration at ~09:20 UTC, but queue growth continues after spike.
nora: posting latest autoscaler logs (truncated):
```
E0901 09:27:12.341 api_autoscaler.go:227] scale loop failed: reconcile error: failed to estimate free_gpus: runtime: out of memory
panic: runtime: out of memory
goroutine 12 [running]:
runtime.throw(0x45fbd1, 0x16)
	/usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:1116 +0x72
	... 
```
satvik: hmm OOM in the autoscaler process itself — that's suspicious. autoscaler should be small footprint.
ingrid: can someone run `kubectl get pods -n redwood-autoscaler -o wide`?
maria: ran it, autoscaler-5c9f8 CrashLoopBackOff on node g4dn-12. current image: autoscaler:v2.4.1.
dmitri: trying `kubectl logs` now to correlate with metrics.
kevin: we should gate traffic if scale isn't coming up. suggestion: switch routing to dedicated-fallback pool in eu-west-1 (dedicated pool has spare capacity).
nora: routing API is `POST /control/reroute` with body `{ "from_pool": "gpu-pool-eu-west-1", "to_pool": "dedicated-fallback-eu-west" }` — who can execute?
maria: I can run that. executing now...
maria: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/reroute -d '{"from_pool":"gpu-pool-eu-west-1","to_pool":"dedicated-fallback-eu-west"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'`
incident-bot: Reroute request accepted. Migrating in-flight requests -> dedicated-fallback-eu-west. Estimated cutover: 30s.
kevin: routing shows 18% of traffic moved so far. queue_depth dropping from 2387 -> 1320 (observed).
dmitri: good, keep that. I'm going to scale the dedicated-fallback pool manual replicas up 2x while we stabilize.
ops-sre: manual scale initiated: `rctl pool scale dedicated-fallback-eu-west --replicas 16`
ops-sre: scaling action completed, new replicas ready.
ingrid: customer impact? which tenants affected and are we notifying them?
kevin: top affected customers: search-api-prod (slo-sensitive), doc-rerank-prod, and a few small startups. error_rate (5xx) peaked at 11.7% for search-api-prod, tail latency > 90th pct > 10s for some requests.
satvik: open support ticket created for VIP customers, CC oncall and account execs.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation progress: queue_depth now 220, avg_latency 210ms, error_rate back to baseline 0.8%. Autoscaler pods still CrashLoopBackOff.
dmitri: root-cause hypothesis: autoscaler memory usage ballooned after recent metrics driver bump (prom-exporter lib) — it collects per-GPU histograms and appears to leak. Need to pin to previous exporter.
kevin: can we roll autoscaler to v2.4.0 which has older exporter pinned?
ops-sre: preparing rollout: `kubectl set image deployment/autoscaler autoscaler=registry.redwood/autoscaler:v2.4.0 -n redwood-autoscaler`
ops-sre: rollout started.
nora: also found a race in scale estimator where large in-flight metrics arrays cause OOM when pool count > 120; we saw pool count at 128 in eu-west due to overprovisioning after partner spike.
ingrid: good note — short-term: patch will be v2.4.2 with a guarded allocation. Long-term: add streaming aggregator to keep memory bounded.
dmitri: autoscaler pods are now restarting healthy on v2.4.0, no OOM. scale loop resuming.
incident-bot: Autoscaler status: Healthy. Scale attempts succeeded, added 8 GPUs to gpu-pool-eu-west-1. Queue drain continuing.
maria: confirming target pools drained. queue_depth -> 12. Latency normalized.
kevin: I'm going to close the urgent customer tickets with a summary and ETA for postmortem.
satvik: scheduling postmortem call for 48h: proposed doc: `/docs/incidents/1725554321-autoscaler-misalloc-postmortem` (will create after thread).
ops-sre: action items (live):
- (A1) Pin autoscaler to safe exporter in hotfix (completed).
- (A2) Add mem-limit + liveness probe to autoscaler pods (in progress).
- (A3) Add alert for autoscaler OOM/CrashLoopBackOff (created, severity=high).
- (A4) Add queue_depth runaway alert at 500 for immediate paging (created).
- (A5) Postmortem and remediation plan (owner: satvik).
dmitri: assigning owners: A1: ops-sre (done), A2: nora, A3: kevin, A4: ingrid, A5: satvik.
nora: I'll open a PR to change estimator to streaming aggregator with a memory cap, link after triage.
ingrid: immediate customer update drafted, can we send now?
kevin: send it. mention root cause as autoscaler memory leak in metrics collector; mitigation manual reroute + hotfix rollback; full postmortem pending.
incident-bot: Incident state => RESOLVED (mitigated). Summary: autoscaler OOM led to scale failures during burst -> queue growth -> partial customer impact (elevated 5xx and high tail latency). Manual failover to dedicated pool + hotfix rollback restored capacity. Postmortem scheduled.
dmitri: great work team. quick retrospective note: we should add a canary for autoscaler on new metric libraries in staging with synthetic load to catch growth.
satvik: adding to A5: add staging canary test + load curve.
maria: thumbs up :thumbsup:.
kevin: closing on-call handoff: i'm staying until 10:00 UTC to monitor, then pass to next oncall per schedule.
ingrid: thanks everyone — please update the incident doc with logs/snippets and link tickets.
incident-bot: Paging history: paged dmitri -> oncall; escalated to ops-sre; notifications sent to infra-sla and customer-ops.
satvik: postmortem doc created at `/incidents/1725554321-autoscaler-memory-leak-postmortem` and assigned to me. I'll include timeline, graphs, and the fix.
kevin: end of thread — closing channel for now.
